stories.text: Crypto firm Binance suffers what is called the largest hack ever, with two analytics firms blaming North Korean hacking unit TraderTraitor.
Erin Patterson, convicted in the Australian mushroom murder case, loses her appeal after three judges reject all seven grounds of unfairness.
Hyrox athlete Joanna Wietrzyk, who soiled herself during a race, accepts responsibility and says she put others at risk but faced excessive backlash.
Whatever the midterm results, Democrats face hard questions about what the party stands for and who should represent it.
Google loses 500 billion dollars in market value, its shares hitting a six-month low after it said AI search summaries were hurting ad revenue.
The penultimate episode of The Traitors features a dramatic confession as the faithful players finally start to apply pressure.
Leaked audio from the Spain train crash suggests a train was cleared to proceed by a control centre although another had stalled on the track.
BBC Verify looks at the cost of the welfare system and the options the government has for cutting spending on it.
Israeli opposition accuses Netanyahu of undermining the election, after his Likud party alleged foreign interference when his coalition lost its majority.
In Serbia, newly elected Student List MPs call for top figures to resign, days after removing Aleksandar Vucic's party from power.
